thread:
Maria K: Kicking off priming for the new sa-west2 cluster tomorrow 04:00 UTC. Need GPU quota reservation + spot fallback plan. I filed the quota request (Q-4721) with perf logs and expected token volumes. Can capacity ops confirm reservation window and expected instance types?
Devin: I see Q-4721 in the console. Cloud responded 'provisional' pending clarifying the burn rate. Uploaded Steady-state and Spike profiles under the request.
Jules: Quick thought — for priming we should do a 24‑hour soft reservation (no billing commit) and a 2‑hour guaranteed hold during bootstrap tests. If health checks pass we convert to a longer commitment. Avoid full annual reserves until we hit steady throughput. :thinking_face:
Leo: +1 for soft reservation first. Also, network egress limits in that region are strict — we need to validate our NAT egress pool and VPN tunnels before we blow GPU cycles.
Sophia: I can run the network sanity tests at 02:00 UTC. What exact checks do you want? latency, MTU, iptables rules, and an end-to-end model pull?
Maria K: Thanks. Target checklist: 1) Reservation confirmed (res id) 2) Image pull / model cache prewarm 3) KV cache warmup run with sample workload 4) Load balancing & LB health checks 5) Traceroute across peering and VPN 6) Cost estimate snapshot.
Devin: For reservation ids, cloud tooling has this command for a hold:
```bash
gcloud compute reservations create res-sa-west2-priming \
  --project=redwood-prod --zone=sa-west2-a \
  --machine-type=a100-80gb --count=8 --start-time="2026-04-08T04:00Z" --end-time="2026-04-09T04:00Z"
```
Note: they might return fewer accelerators; we should list fallback SKUs.
Jules: I'll file a smaller fallback reservation: 4x v100/80gb equivalent spot mix. If any SKU mismatch, capacity service will auto-map and we get a notification.
capacity-bot: Reservation created (soft): res-2026-04-sa-west2-priming — expires 2026-04-09T04:00Z — reserved GPUs: 8 (requested), fallback mapped: [v100-80gb, a10x-40gb].
Leo: Network checklist snippet (for Sophia):
```text
- verify NAT IP pool size >= concurrent pulls (default 25)
- test VPN tunnel throughput (iperf3)
- MTU probe across peering (ping -M do -s)
- ensure node SGs allow model registry egress 443/4433
```
Sophia: Running iperf3 between our edge and sa-west2 at 02:00 UTC. I'll post results. Also will validate route preference — we had a case where egress took intercontinental path once.
Devin: On cost — priming burn estimate: ~2.4k USD for 24h at full capacity (a100 class). If we use spot fallback for 50% of fleet we drop to ~1.1k USD but risk churn. Include that in the handoff doc.
Maria K: Good. During priming we'll run these validation jobs:
- small inference smoke (1k tokens/s for 30m)
- KV cache warmup with 24h trace replay (low concurrency)
- end-to-end SLO test (90th latency under 400ms for 512 tokens)

Please add run ids back here once queued.
Jules: I've added canary job templates to the runbook and a quick abort script:
```bash
# abort priming gracefully
kubectl scale deployment/priming-worker --replicas=0 -n redwood-priming
# drain nodes
gcloud compute instances reset --zone=sa-west2-a --instances $(cat /tmp/node-list)
```
Sophia: iperf3 results: TCP 9.3Gbps sustained, no major packet loss. MTU OK. NAT pool needs increase to 40 for concurrent pulls, filed NAT-INC-98.
Devin: Cloud replied to Q-4721: approved for provisional quota 8 GPUs for 24h window, please provide expected sustained hours for next 30 days to move to commit.
Maria K: We'll hand off to capacity + finance after priming. Action items: 1) Capacity confirm res mapping (Jules) 2) Network NAT increase (Sophia) 3) Run priming jobs and post run ids (Devin) 4) Cost snapshot & commit recommendation (Maria) 5) SRE oncall to monitor traces (Leo).
Leo: I'll be oncall during priming window and will enable extra tracing hooks. If latency SLO fails, we fallback to regional model variant and scale down batch size.
Jules: Reservation and fallback procedures documented under /runbooks/sa-west2-priming. I also added a checklist for 'nonblocking handoff' to capacity that lists minimal telemetry we need to accept a longer commit.
Maria K: Perfect. Tagging @capacity-bot when priming starts and again when it's healthy. :rocket:
capacity-bot: Reminder scheduled: 2026-04-08T03:50Z — will post start confirmation in this thread.
